name: IRF3205PBF
title: 55 V, 110 A N-channel HEXFET power MOSFET in TO-220
summary: A single N-channel power MOSFET rated 55 V drain to source, with an on-resistance of at most 8.0 mΩ at VGS = 10 V and 62 A. Continuous drain current is 110 A at a 25 °C case as calculated from junction temperature, held to 75 A by the TO-220 package. It is avalanche rated (62 A, 20 mJ repetitive), handles a junction temperature up to 175 °C and dissipates up to 200 W at a 25 °C case. The leads are lead-free.

circuits.title: Switching time test circuit (Fig. 10)
circuits.description: A 10 V gate pulse through RG switches the transistor against a resistive drain load RD fed from VDD. The pulse is no wider than 1 µs and its duty factor at most 0.1 %. VGS at the gate and VDS at the drain are watched together; td(on), tr, td(off) and tf are taken between the 10 % and 90 % points of the two waveforms.

circuits.title: Fig. 12a Unclamped inductive test circuit
circuits.description: The avalanche test. A gate pulse of width tp through RG turns the device under test on, and current builds in inductor L from VDD through a high-side driver transistor. When the gate pulse ends the drain flies up to V(BR)DSS and the stored energy is dumped into the device while the current IAS, read across the 0.01 Ω resistor, falls to zero. A diode runs from the return up to the junction of L and the driver.

circuits.title: Fig. 13b Gate charge test circuit
circuits.description: A 3 mA current pulse charges the gate of the device under test while a second transistor of the same type, held at a fixed gate bias, acts as a current regulator in its drain from the VDS supply. The gate bias comes from a 12 V battery through a 50 kΩ potentiometer, decoupled by 0.2 µF across the battery and 0.3 µF on the wiper, all referred to the regulator's source. Two current-sampling resistors in the ground returns measure IG and ID; VGS is watched at the gate to read Qgs, Qgd and Qg.

circuits.title: Fig. 14 Peak diode recovery dv/dt test circuit
circuits.description: Tests the body diode of the device under test, whose gate is tied to its source. A driver transistor of the same type, gated through RG, pulls current from VDD through a current-sense resistor and an inductor; when the driver turns off the inductor current freewheels through a low-leakage current transformer and the body diode back to VDD. When the driver turns on again the diode recovers, and RG sets the dv/dt of the drain. The duty factor D = pulse width / period sets ISD, with an inductor ripple of at most 5 %. Layout needs low stray inductance and a ground plane. The gate drive is 10 V (5 V for logic-level devices).

operation.text: The silicon would carry 110 A continuously at a 25 °C case before reaching its junction temperature limit, but the TO-220 package limits continuous current to 75 A. Fig. 9 shows both limits against case temperature: the package limit stays at 75 A up to about 102 °C, after which the junction temperature limit takes over and the allowed current falls to zero at 175 °C.

The device is rated for repetitive avalanche at 62 A and 20 mJ, with the pulse width set by the maximum junction temperature. A single avalanche pulse from TJ = 25 °C with 138 µH and 62 A is rated at 264 mJ, a calculated figure bounded by TJ = 175 °C; typical parts are destroyed only at about 1050 mJ. Fig. 12c gives the single-pulse energy against starting junction temperature for 25 A, 44 A and 62 A.

Delays and transition times are measured between the 10 % and 90 % points of the gate and drain waveforms: td(on) from VGS rising through 10 % to VDS falling through 90 %, tr from 90 % to 10 % of VDS, td(off) from VGS falling through 90 % to VDS rising through 10 %, and tf from 10 % to 90 % of VDS.

With a constant gate current, VGS rises to a plateau (charge Qgs), stays on the plateau while the drain swings (charge Qgd), then climbs again to the drive voltage; the total charge to that point is QG. At ID = 62 A the plateau sits near 5.3 V.

Surface-mount assembly of the TO-220 is not recommended. It is fixed with a 6-32 or M3 screw at up to 10 lbf·in (1.1 N·m); leads may be soldered at 300 °C for 10 seconds 1.6 mm from the case. The flat greased case-to-sink interface adds 0.50 °C/W typical.

The package carries the part number on the first line, then the Infineon logo with a code HYWWX, where H marks halogen-free, Y is the year, WW the week and X the assembly site, and a four-digit assembly lot code on the last line.
